default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1138.title: Round-number crossing follow
E-1138.hypothesis: Index levels at multiples of 250/500/1000 points attract resting stops and breakout orders; a bar that closes through one in its own direction triggers them and the move should continue briefly.

E-1139.title: Dollar-leads-index lag
E-1139.hypothesis: Index and dollar move inversely; when the mini dollar makes an outsized move and the index has not yet responded, slower index participants catch up in the opposite direction.

E-1140.title: Session-midpoint cross follow
E-1140.hypothesis: Once the day's range is wide relative to yesterday's, a close crossing the range midpoint shifts the balance of the auction toward the new side; follow it.

E-1141.title: Prior-close cross after a hold
E-1141.hypothesis: The prior settlement is the reference for the day's winners and losers; after trading on one side for a while, a close across it flips positioning and traders chase.

E-1142.title: Staircase bars follow
E-1142.hypothesis: Several consecutive bars with both higher highs and higher lows (or lower/lower) show persistent one-sided order flow; the sequence onset is followed.

E-1143.title: Lunch-range break
E-1143.hypothesis: Liquidity thins into the midday lull and reopens with New York around 13:00; a close beyond the lunch range marks the afternoon's direction as sidelined participants return.

E-1144.title: Absorption bar reversal
E-1144.hypothesis: A high-volume bar with a small range after a sharp move means aggressive orders were absorbed by passive size; the move that preceded it tends to reverse.

E-1145.title: EMA ribbon alignment onset
E-1145.hypothesis: When fast, medium and slow EMAs line up in order with price beyond the fast one, short- and medium-term holders agree on direction; the first alignment bar starts a continuation.

E-1147.title: Window-extreme recovery through the midpoint
E-1147.hypothesis: After a rolling window's low (high) was set recently, a close back through the window midpoint shows buyers (sellers) recovered half the range and continuing is favoured.

E-1146.title: Index-leads-dollar lag
E-1146.hypothesis: The mini dollar often reacts to index moves with a delay; after an outsized index move with the dollar still unmoved, the dollar follows inversely.
